personas.name: Gunnar
personas.hidden_agenda: Wrote the script that introduced the error, years ago

personas.name: Leila
personas.hidden_agenda: Afraid this will cost her the recommendation letter she needs

personas.name: Kai
personas.goals: Keep the field season on track
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been talking to another lab about switching

personas.name: Hester
personas.goals: Logistics that work and a lab that isn't miserable
personas.hidden_agenda: Knows Kai is thinking of leaving

pack.title: Alpine ecology lab meeting

agenda.title: The dataset errors
agenda.goal: Understand the errors Leila found in the published dataset

agenda.title: The correction
agenda.goal: Decide how to correct the record

agenda.title: The lab
agenda.goal: Talk about how people are doing

facts.statement: Records affected by the unit error = 312
Journal asks for corrections within 30 days of notice

beats.summary: What Leila found; Gunnar minimizes it
How to fix the record; the citation count corrected
Huts, helicopters and loggers; Kai's helicopter figure is low and is corrected; Hester's logger count stands

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Leila, you sent an email about the dataset. Let's hear it, briefly.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: Some of the soil temperature records were converted twice. Fahrenheit to Celsius, and then again. They're wrong in the published data.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: How many records are we talking about? A handful?

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Is it the old logger script? The one from twenty sixteen?

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: Yes. It's three hundred and twelve records, out of ninety-eight hundred.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: So about fifty that matter, realistically. The rest are in winter, when nothing grows.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: All three hundred and twelve are wrong, Gunnar. They're in the published file.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Three percent of the data. It doesn't change the conclusions.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: It changes figure four. The warming trend is smaller once you fix them.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: How much smaller?

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: The trend drops by about a third. It's still there, but it's weaker.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: The paper has over a hundred citations. People rely on it.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: That's exactly why it matters, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Nobody asked you, Kai.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: Gunnar. That's not okay.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: I'm sorry. Kai, I'm sorry. This is my paper, and it's hard to hear.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: The journal wants corrections within thirty days of notice. I think we notify them now.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Or we fix it quietly in the next paper.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: Quietly isn't an option. The data are public.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: I checked the journal page while you were talking, Gunnar. It's forty-one citations, not over a hundred.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Forty-one. It felt like more.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Forty-one people who used the wrong numbers.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: All right. All right. We notify the journal this week and publish a correction with the fixed data.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: Thank you. I'll draft the correction notice and the corrected figure.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: I'll write to the editor myself. It should come from me, as the senior author.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Should we tell the people who cited it?

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: The journal notifies them automatically when a correction is published.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: Fieldwork. We start on July seventh. Eighteen hut nights are booked.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: And two helicopter lifts, at about two thousand each.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: The loggers did well last winter. We recovered all sixty.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Good. The loggers are the whole study.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Can we afford a third lift, for the high plots?

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: The grant balance is forty-one thousand. A lift is cheap compared to losing a season.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: Did anyone else see the avalanche video from the pass last week? The whole slope just went.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: The guides posted it. It's terrifying.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: That's the slope right above the second hut.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: Sorry, I'm looking at the invoice from last year. The helicopter was thirty-two hundred a lift, not two thousand.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Thirty-two hundred. That changes the math a bit.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: We still book the third lift. I'd rather pay than risk the high plots.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: I'll call the helicopter company tomorrow and add the third lift.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: It might be worth someone checking the second hut is safe after that avalanche.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: Last thing. I want to ask how everyone's doing. It's been a hard few weeks.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Honestly? Not great. I've been thinking about whether this lab is right for me.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Because of today?

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Partly. Partly before today.

turns.speaker: Leila
turns.text: I was scared to raise the error at all. I thought it might cost me my reference letter.

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: It won't. Finding it was the right thing. I should have said that first.

turns.speaker: Hester
turns.text: Can we have a lab lunch next week, no agenda, just to talk?

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Yes. Please. I'll pay for it.

turns.speaker: Kai
turns.text: Will the correction affect my thesis chapter that uses the same data?

turns.speaker: Gunnar
turns.text: Thank you, all of you. Especially you, Leila.
